section_summary: This section covers proposals to reduce Occupation controls over Japan’s economy, alongside reports on trade, exports, currency, tourism, investment, and economic administration in August and September 1949. It also contains David M. Maynard’s recommendations on current Japanese economic problems, an exchange about assistance to Iran, and several routing and record-copy sheets.

subfiles.title: Progressive Decontrol of the Economy of Japan, concluding pages
subfiles.about: Maynard recommends a timetable for reducing Occupation economic controls and staff.
subfiles.summary: The report argues that continued detailed guidance by General Headquarters inhibits Japanese responsibility. It proposes substantial personnel cuts by 1951 and a smaller State Department economic staff to advise, inspect, and report.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tokyo’s despatch 544
subfiles.about: Summarizes Maynard’s recommendations for Japanese economic self-support and reduced American controls.
subfiles.summary: Reedy summarizes Maynard’s decontrol proposal and proposed economic staff for a future ambassador.

subfiles.title: Tokyo airgram on economic and trade developments
subfiles.about: Reports trade concerns, foreign agency plans, private imports, and deconcentration reporting.
subfiles.summary: The badly damaged airgram discusses Japan’s export outlook, sterling-area purchases, foreign offices for Japanese firms, private import trade, and a pending deconcentration report. Its first pages are too damaged to establish every point securely.

subfiles.title: Clearance of attached airgram on industrial concentration
subfiles.about: Recommends withholding an airgram questioning concentration of production in efficient Japanese plants.
subfiles.summary: The writer says efficient allocation of scarce materials need not conflict with deconcentration and warns that the proposed inquiry could encourage renewed dispersal of production among inefficient plants.

subfiles.title: Clearance of Japan economic information survey
subfiles.about: Returns a Japan economic survey with research division comments.
subfiles.summary: Fearey returns the survey and Warren Hunsberger’s comments for consideration.

subfiles.title: Tokyo airgram A-206 on economic developments
subfiles.about: Reports SCAP discussions of stabilization, tourism, trade, foreign business rules, and sterling-area negotiations.
subfiles.summary: The airgram covers a held-up Dodge letter, proposed larger banknotes, preparations for Voorhees’s visit, tourist receipts, Japanese attendance at an ECAFE meeting, export-bazaar textiles, Taiwan sugar, technicians’ travel, revisions to foreign-business licensing, and lagging sterling-area talks.

subfiles.title: Tokyo airgram A-212 on economic developments
subfiles.about: Reports economic administration, currency, loans, trade arrangements, and export-policy debates.
subfiles.summary: The airgram describes reorganization of the Economic and Scientific Section, export bottlenecks, coal decontrol, approval of 1,000-yen notes, proposed counterpart-fund loan rates, Taiwan sugar, arbitration, and licences for American lawyers. It also discusses Japanese export associations, sterling-area negotiations, barter imports, a German trade arrangement, and possible textile sales in the Middle East.

subfiles.title: Note requesting reply on Iranian assistance
subfiles.about: Requests a reply to the attached Iranian letter.
subfiles.summary: Asks whether Iran’s requests have been identified or answered.

subfiles.title: Letter concerning economic and military assistance to Iran
subfiles.about: Urges greater U.S. economic and military assistance to Iran.
subfiles.summary: The Iranian ambassador seeks clarification of U.S. intentions and argues that assistance would strengthen public confidence and Iran’s resistance to aggression and communism. The handwritten OCR is substantially damaged.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of report on public relations aspects of stabilization
subfiles.to: Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards a research report on public relations and Japan’s stabilization program.
subfiles.summary: Forwards two copies and invites comments after discussion with appropriate SCAP officials.

subfiles.title: Reply to Ambassador Ala
subfiles.about: Proposes a discussion of pending U.S.–Iranian matters when Ala returns to Washington.
subfiles.summary: McGhee acknowledges misunderstandings and proposes talks on economic and military assistance.

subfiles.title: Despatch 599 and enclosure on current problems in Japan, damaged copy
subfiles.from: U.S. Political Adviser, Tokyo; David M. Maynard
subfiles.about: Transmits Maynard’s recommendations on current Japanese economic problems.
subfiles.summary: This damaged copy covers trade, prices, imports, tariffs, and Maynard’s view that Japan’s condition was less dire than some statistics suggested. A clearer record copy follows on pages 610–613.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tokyo despatch 599
subfiles.about: Comments on Maynard’s economic recommendations, especially labor policy.
subfiles.summary: Recommends reading Maynard’s memorandum but questions his proposed review of labor policy.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement sheet for Tokyo despatch 599
subfiles.about: Designates a replacement record copy of Tokyo despatch 599.
subfiles.summary: Records that the original action copy was not returned.

subfiles.title: Despatch 599 transmitting Maynard’s Current Problems in Japan
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Political Adviser, Tokyo; David M. Maynard
subfiles.about: Transmits Maynard’s August 8 memorandum recommending changes to Japanese economic policy.
subfiles.summary: Maynard calls for removing floor prices, expanding private imports and shipping, revising tariffs, liberalizing foreign investment, and establishing a claims commission. He also recommends reviewing labor rules, maintaining Dodge’s balanced-budget program, easing some controls and travel restrictions, and treating pessimistic economic statistics cautiously.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement sheet for Tokyo airgram A-215
subfiles.about: Designates a replacement record copy of Tokyo airgram A-215.
subfiles.summary: Records that the original action copy was not returned.

subfiles.title: Tokyo airgram A-215 on economic and trade developments
subfiles.about: Reports trade issues involving copper, sterling-area goods, Siam, Korea, Sweden, and the Netherlands.
subfiles.summary: The airgram discusses possible Japanese copper sales, returned Chinese narcotics, preparations for Voorhees’s visit, and a proposal to curtail sterling-area entrepot trade. It also reports possible dollar trade with Siam, a proposed Japan–Korea trade review, and credit and payment issues involving Sweden and the Netherlands.
